verses.1: And the children of Israel went forth and camped at Moab, beyond the Jordan, at Jericho.
verses.2: And Balak, son of Zippor, saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
verses.3: Moaab was driven away from before the people, because he was too many in number. Moaab was also rejected by the children of Israel.
verses.4: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now let the people go and explore all the surrounding areas. Let them see the fields and the land that belongs to King Sion.”
verses.5: And he sent demons to Bilam, son of Beor Pethora. These demons were from the people living by the river in the land of Israel. They were sent to say to Bilam, “Look! The people have left Egypt. Now they will rule over this land.”
verses.6: And now, please tell me about this people. They seem to be trying to get away from me. I can’t do anything about them. I’ll be forced to leave this land. I know what you will say: “Blessed be those who bless you.”
verses.7: And the elders of Moab and Midian went there, carrying swords in their hands. They came to Balak and spoke to him those words of Balaq.
verses.8: And he said to them, “Come here tonight. I will tell you what Jehovah has commanded me to say.” Then the priests of Moab sat down with the people.
verses.9: And God came to Bileam and said, “Who are these people who are with you?”
verses.10: And Bilam said to the Lord, “Balaq, son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me.”
verses.11: Look, the people who came from Egypt have now covered the land with their eyes. Now it’s time for me to take action against them, so that they won’t be able to fight against me anymore.
verses.12: And God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. Do not show your face in their presence, for they are blessed.”
verses.13: And in the morning, he arose and said to the officers of Balaam, “Go back to your land. For what does Jehovah want me to go with you?”
verses.14: And the officers of Moab arose and went to Balaam. They said, “What do you think? Should we go with them?”
verses.15: And Balak gathered together many leaders and powerful men from among them.
verses.16: And they went to Balaam. They said to him, “Balaam, son of BethEhuzabim, please do not go with us.”
verses.17: For I will bring you great sorrow, and everything you say to me, I will do. Please, allow me to deal with this people myself.
verses.18: And Balaam said to the servants of Balak, “If Balak gives me gold and silver in exchange for doing this or that, it will not please the LORD, my God, to allow me to do such a small or great thing.”
verses.19: And now, let us all sit down for the night. May I know what Jehovah will say to me.
verses.20: And God came to Bilam one night. He said to him, “If those people call for your help, then go with them. But what I am about to tell you, you must do.”
verses.21: And in the morning, Bileam stood up and cast his own son into the fire. Then he went away with the men of Moab.
verses.22: And God’s face turned red as he walked along. Jehovah stood on the road to Satan. He rode on his back, along with his two sons.
verses.23: And the oxen saw the hand of the LORD standing in the road, with its horn in its hand. The oxen stepped aside from the road, and they ran into the field. They trampled the oxen underfoot, so that they could not cross the road anymore.
verses.24: And the angel of the LORD stood in the vineyard. This vineyard belonged to him, and that vineyard also belonged to him.
verses.25: And the angel saw the temple of Jehovah. He rushed towards it, and he pressed his feet against the wall. Then it was filled with dust.
verses.26: And the servant of Jehovah increased in number, and he stood in a place where there was no way to turn right or left.
verses.27: And the serpent saw God’s angel. It rushed down into the pit, and it bit the angel’s ear. Then it was caught in the trap.
verses.28: And Jehovah opened His mouth, and He said to Bilam, “What have I done to you? For you killed those three legs.”
verses.29: And Bileam said to his brother, “You have wronged me. I have nothing left in my hands to fight back against you. Now, you will die.”
verses.30: And the angel said to Bilam, “Do not be angry with me. I have been riding on your back from that day until today. I have suffered greatly to do what you wanted me to do.” And Bilam said, “No.”
verses.31: And Jehovah revealed the eyes of Beelzebub. He saw that Jehovah’s angel stood on the road, with his sword in his hand. Then he bowed down and worshipped at his feet.
verses.32: And Melchizedek said to him, “How can you do this? You have a six-legged animal. Now, I will go and hunt for food, just as I always do.”
verses.33: And I saw that creature. It stood before me, with three legs. But I turned away from it, because now I have killed you too, and I’ve kept her alive.
verses.34: And Bileam said to the angel of the LORD, “My sin is that I did not know that you were standing ready to speak to me. Now, if it is wrong in your eyes, then I will return.”
verses.35: And the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the people. I will cancel what I have spoken to you.” So Balaam went with the men of Balak.
verses.36: And Balak heard that Bileam had come. So he went out to meet him in the city of Moab, which was on the border of Arnon, at the end of the border.
verses.37: And Balak said to Bileam, “Have I not sent you to speak to you? Why didn’t you go to me? I truly don’t understand why you didn’t do as I commanded you.”
verses.38: And Bilam said to Balak, “Now I have come to you. Now may I speak what God has given me to say.”
verses.39: And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath Jotzath.
verses.40: And Balak offered sacrifices to Baal, as well as to the goat idols. He also sent them to Bileam and to the priests who served those idols.
verses.41: In the morning, he took Bilam with him. They went up to the mountain, and from there he saw the end of the people.
